subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget, tombstone/supersede, and conflict resolution across memory plugins?
rationale: The code gap is real, but the correct solution depends on durable storage, privacy, rollback, review UX, plugin API, migration, and multi-plugin compatibility choices that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

options.title: Narrow v1 to memory-core
options.body: Implement review/edit/forget/conflict behavior only for bundled memory-core first, accepting a later API alignment step for external memory plugins.

options.title: Defer lifecycle MVP
options.body: Keep current search, promotion, Dreaming, and Memory Wiki behavior while concrete stale-memory bugs remain tracked separately.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage/schema and SDK history makes this the best available routing candidate for lifecycle contract direction.
